title: Relayed yes reaches the session: genlock tell --relay-yes is recorded so the session's --relayed launch/swap finds it

requirements.text: A yes Tally passes with genlock tell --relay-yes is recorded where the target session's genlock launch/swap --relayed finds it, including when the tell goes through a project's Subassistant
requirements.check: a test relays a yes to a session and its launch --relayed succeeds, and a session with no relayed yes is still refused

evidence: Cause: app relayToAssistant() -> peekRelays() read relay-yes.json in every session folder as a report, failed to decode, deleted it (Voice.swift:707). Fix: grant renamed yes-relayed.json (lib/relay.mjs), peekRelays skips relay-yes.json, launch yes reusable 15 min. tests/run.mjs 584/584 incl. 'no yes relayed is refused', 'yes relayed opens the pane', new 'same launch yes covers a second launch' (fails with reuse off: 583/584); swift testRelayPickupLeavesARelayedYesAlone passes, swift test 156/0 failures. App installed and relaunched 18:2x with fix.

answers.observed: relay-yes.json absent from main's channel after the 22:46 tell that printed Passed; Voice.swift peekRelays filter hasPrefix(relay-) && hasSuffix(.json) matches it and removeItem on decode failure
answers.cause: inferred from code, not watched live: the deletion happened before I looked; the filter + delete path is certain, the timing (app poll before session's command) is the hypothesis
answers.absence: grant file not found by ls in the target folder; folder is the one the message came through
answers.assumption: that the Subassistant tell resolved to the same session the writer ran in; its message text proves the grant was written to the folder that delivered it
answers.falsify: a live relay after restart where --relayed is still refused would falsify it
